name: Clean Water Saints
description: One of the earliest neural-feed blockbusters produced by Vantablack Media's infrastructure subsidiary, depicting a heroic team of GLMZ engineers racing to restore water filtration to the lower tiers after a catastrophic sabotage event. The film is widely understood to be a fictionalized inversion of the 2183 HelixCorp water infrastructure scandal, with the real corporate saboteurs recast as Shelf-dwelling terrorists. Budget of Φ180 million; won four Vantablack Meridian Awards.
cultural_impact: Established the template for the 'infrastructure heroism' genre that dominated early neural-feed cinema, and made the erasure of corporate culpability through spectacle a normalized practice.
story_hooks: An archivist has located the original whistleblower report from 2183 that the film was designed to bury — it names specific HelixCorp executives still active in 2226
A character who appears briefly in the film as an unnamed Shelf victim is based on a real person who was paid Φ200 and signed away their likeness — and is still alive
The film's director, who died in 2201, left behind a private neural recording that his estate is now trying to suppress
